newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian, Luxembourg bourses discuss data link.
newsitem.headline: Belgian, Luxembourg bourses discuss data link.

text.p: The Brussels and Luxembourg stock exchanges are discussing ways to link their two price quotation systems, giving their members remote access to their respective markets, officials from the two bourses said.

"I can confirm a protocol was concluded between the bourse last October. This aims above all at cooperation on a technical level: it would allow our respective members to have access to the markets of the other bourse," Brussels Stock Exchange executive Dominique Valschaerts told Reuters on Tuesday.

"There's no question of a merger. The agreements relate mainly to technical issues, targeting activities where we are not in competition and looking to bring economies of scale on certain costs to members," Luxembourg Stock Exchange Chairman Remy Kremer said at its annual "bourse day" on Monday.

Valschaerts said the move was being driven by requests from the bourses' members and was within the context of the European Investment Services Directive (ISD), which entered into force on January 1, 1996.
Valschaerts said initial studies had shown it should be possible to have data feeds connecting the two markets despite the fact each uses a different trading platform.
"There's no reason why we should not be able to come to a conclusion by the end of (1997)," Valschaerts added.
